title: messaging-plays-ml-backend-platform-adaptations
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact set of high-impact messaging plays and demo scripts tailored to three adjacent technical personas: ML engineers, backend engineers, and platform teams. It’s written for reps, content writers, and product marketers who need quick, persona-specific language and proof points for workshops, blog hooks, and demo flows.

Topline position (single-sentence):
Redwood Inference is the inference runtime and control plane that makes production LLM serving predictable — low-latency at scale, cost-controllable, and safe-to-rollout across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.

Persona summaries (one-liners to use in subject lines / intros):
- ML engineers: "Ship model-quality with predictable inference economics — improved latency and cost without compromising evals."
- Backend engineers: "Integrate a high-throughput, low-latency API that behaves like any other enterprise service (SLOs, retries, SDKs)."
- Platform teams: "Standardize inference across teams with governance, capacity guarantees, and per-route observability."

Core pillars mapped to persona (3 bullets each):
- ML engineers (focus: fidelity + reproducibility):
  • Model parity and versioning: pin versions, roll back, and reproduce outputs across environments.
  • Quality-safe optimizations: automatic quantization and caching suggestions tied to evaluation sets so you don’t regress.
  • Eval and drift hooks: integrated eval pipelines and regression alerts by prompt set.
- Backend engineers (focus: latency + reliability):
  • Predictable latency SLOs: dedicated capacity, routing policies, and graceful fallback on overload.
  • Runtime ergonomics: SDKs + streaming + idempotent retries and backpressure semantics.
  • Cost & throughput controls: batching policies and autoscale settings exposed as knobs.
- Platform teams (focus: governance + ops):
  • Access & audit: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and RBAC for routes and models.
  • Observability: token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency heatmaps, and rollout tracing.
  • Policy-driven routing: route by cost/region/SLA and automated fallback policies for availability.

Proof points & meaningful metrics to surface per persona:
- ML engineers: published evals showing <2% change in top-1 LM score after quantization + A/B rollback in <5 minutes.
- Backend engineers: p50/p90/p99 token latency numbers for benchmarked models; e.g., p50=18ms, p95=46ms on ded. capacity (example).
- Platform teams: show multi-tenant cost delta — 30% unit-cost reduction vs naive single-request inference via batching + cache.

Competitive framing & short counters (talk tracks):
- Versus API-first LLM vendors: "We match ease-of-use but add deterministic economics and enterprise rollouts — less surprise bills and predictable degradations."
- Versus self-hosted runtimes: "You keep control without the ops debt: we provide consistent routing, SLOs, and a controlled private installation option."
- Versus cloud-managed endpoints (general cloud): "More inference-first optimizations (KV caching, kernel selection), and model-level rollout primitives built-in."

Objection handlers (rapid answers sales can memorize):
- "We already use another provider for embeddings/generation": Redwood supports multi-model routing and can act as a drop-in runtime for specific routes while you maintain the rest.
- "We can't risk quality regressions with quantization": We attach quantization recommendations to baseline evals and provide canary rollouts + automated quality alerts on your prompt set before changes are promoted.
- "We need air-gapped/on-prem control": Redwood Private provides a customer-controlled control plane option and appliance for air-gapped deployments with KMS/HSM integrations.

Demo scripts (30–45 minute technical demo flows by persona):
- ML engineer demo highlights:
  1) Show model upload and version pin.
  2) Run a small eval set; show baseline metrics.
  3) Apply suggested quantization profile; run eval and show metrics side-by-side.
  4) Create canary rollout (10% traffic) and demonstrate automatic rollback on regression.
  Key slides: eval dashboard, diff view, rollback timeline.
- Backend engineer demo highlights:
  1) Show REST + SDK integration and a streaming trace.
  2) Configure autoscale + burst policy; run a synthetic load to show behavior.
  3) Trigger fallback: simulate capacity pressure and show routing to cheaper model variant.
  Key slides: latency dashboard, per-route SLO config, SDK snippet.
- Platform team demo highlights:
  1) Show multi-team routing policy and RBAC for model routes.
  2) Walk through a compliance audit log and KMS key usage.
  3) Show cost explorer with per-token breakdown and a policy-based budget alert.
  Key slides: governance page, cost explorer, rollout policy editor.

Sample email outreach snippets (A/B test candidates):
- ML engineer A: "Cut inference costs without retraining: quick quantization + eval guardrails"
- ML engineer B: "Pin versions, run safe rollouts, and detect regressions on real prompts"
- Backend engineer A: "SLA-first inference — stable latency, predictable autoscaling"
- Platform team A: "Centralize inference policies: RBAC, cost controls, and auditability"

Short code example to include in docs/web (plain text):
- SDK example (pseudo):
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key)
  resp = client.generate(model='open-llama-7b', prompt='Summarize the following...')
  // stream tokens, check token-cost header

Channel & content tactics per persona (where to invest):
- ML engineers: technical blog deep dives (quantization/eval), reproducible notebooks, benchmarks repo, community Slack/OSS integrations.
- Backend engineers: quickstart SDK guides, sample services + K6/locust load tests, one-click Heroku/GCP quickstarts.
- Platform teams: whitepapers on governance, TCO calculators, enterprise customer case studies focused on policy+cost wins.

Battle-card one-liners for SDRs (30–60s talk tracks):
- ML engineer: "We let teams lower per-token cost and automate guardrails so MLOps can focus on models, not servicing headaches."
- Backend engineer: "Treat inference like any other production API — predictable SLOs, retries, and SDKs for polyglot services."
- Platform: "A single control plane for teams to enforce budgets, RBAC, and rollout policies across hosted/dedicated/private footprints."

10-minute checklist for a successful POC (cross-persona):
1) Agree on 2–3 target prompts / eval set.
2) Baseline latency + quality metrics.
3) Define SLOs and budget per route.
4) Configure canary and rollback thresholds.
5) Run traffic simulation and observe tracing & cost.
6) Document final model/profile and hand off to ops.

Open questions & follow-ups for product: (notes for PMs/engineering)
- Expose an API to sync org eval suites; make it easier to import benchmark results automatically.
- Add a "quick-simulate" mode for platform teams to preview cost impact of route changes before applying.
- Improve demo-ready datasets for each persona (small, focused, reproducible).

Attachments & next steps:
- Owner: Asha Kapoor (GTM) — sync with Priya Nair (content) & Ethan Morales (solutions) to build:
  • three 2-page one-pagers (one per persona),
  • two demo recordings (ML engineer + platform),
  • a public benchmark notebook.

Notes on tone and vocabulary (quick style guide):
- ML engineers: precise, experiment-driven language ("A/B", "eval set", "regression").
- Backend engineers: systems language, SLOs, latency percentiles, error budgets.
- Platform teams: governance, RBAC, auditability, cost policies, SLA language.

End of doc.
